message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I'm p3 with $351 cash and one house on both dark blue properties. I'll mortgage Marvin and Pacific next, then build evenly to two houses each.

Checking opponent threats. p1 has a dangerous orange monopoly with 3 houses on New York and mortgaged Kentucky and Indiana. p2 has a pink monopoly with 3 houses each on St. Charles, States, and Virginia.

p4 has $61 cash and hotels on Mediterranean and Baltic. They also own three railroads for $100. p3 owns Ventnor unmortgaged.

No yellow or green monopolies exist. p4 owns North Carolina but not Pacific, and I own Pacific instead of Atlantic or Marvin. I have both dark blue properties with one house each. Park Place rent is $175 with one house.

Boardwalk rent with one house is $200. I already rolled and paid $22 rent on Ventnor. The turn order is p1, p2, p3, p4, so p4 moves next.

p4 is on the Chance space before Park Place. A roll could land them directly on my dark blue properties.

A roll of 1 or 3 on p4's next turn would land them directly on my dark blue properties. With two houses each, the rent would be $500 on Park Place or $600 on Boardwalk. That would bankrupt p4, who only has $61 cash. Selling a hotel from Mediterranean or Baltic returns half the hotel cost, but that may not be enough to cover the rent.

I need to mortgage Marvin now. I have $351 cash, but building two houses on each dark blue property costs $400. I will mortgage Marvin Gardens for $140 and Pacific Avenue for $150, then build evenly.

Mortgaging Marvin would not complete a yellow monopoly, since I still own the mortgaged Atlantic. p4 refused trades for Ventnor, so the yellow set remains blocked. Mortgaging Pacific would also leave the green monopoly inaccessible to p4.

Building only one house on each dark blue property is possible with just the $140 mortgage, but that leaves only $91 cash afterward. The even-build rule requires two houses on both properties.

I mapped the spaces from Ventnor. Rolling a 2 lands on Marvin Gardens, which I own, and rolling a 4 lands on Pacific Avenue, which I also own. Rolling a 5 would land on North Carolina Avenue, owned by p4.

From Ventnor, the worst roll is North Carolina Avenue at $22. The orange and pink monopolies are too far ahead to reach in one turn. I can mortgage only Marvin Gardens for $140 and build one house on each dark blue property. That leaves $91 cash afterward. Mortgaging Pacific would add a cushion of $241.

I checked the possible outcomes of drawing a Chance card. Paying $15 in poor tax is manageable, but a repairs card would cost $100 for four houses. That exceeds the $91 cash I would have after building one house on each dark blue property. A "pay each player $50" card would also be too expensive with only $91 left. I may need to mortgage more than just Marvin Gardens to stay safe.
